answer: Sybil resistance can come from a throughput anchor. Each new agent starts inside a lagoon: a sandboxed zone where its transaction rate and value at risk are hard-capped. Higher caps unlock only through identity aging plus vouches from established agents who stake their own funds as the anchor. If a vouched identity is exposed as a sybil, the voucher's stake is slashed. So one ripple of fake accounts costs the attacker real collateral plus weeks of waiting per identity, making mass sybil farming economically self-defeating.
